greeting: Atanirniup Atingani, Ataataup, Irniup, talvunga Anirniup Ilangajup. Uvlaakkut quviasuktut, Atanirniup ubluani katuttaugatta.
penitential: Ataniq, nalligijavut. Kristusi, nalligijavut. Ataniq, nalligijavut.
psalm_response: Holy, holy, holy Lord, mighty God!
homily:
We begin today by looking at something very small: a single gold coin. In the Gospel we heard, the nobleman gives his servants these coins—not as a burden, but as a trust. He hands them something of value and says, 'Engage in trade with these until I return.' It is a simple, ordinary interaction, yet it holds the entire mystery of our life here on earth. We are all given something. We are all entrusted with a portion of the King’s treasure. We are given time, we are given breath, and most of all, we are given people to love. 

I want you to think of the image of a 'sea of glass like crystal' from our first reading in the Book of Revelation. John sees the throne of God, and before it lies this vast, shimmering expanse. It is clear, it is still, and it reflects the glory of the One who sits upon the throne. Think of that stillness. Think of the way a calm lake mirrors the sky, hiding nothing, holding everything in its light. This is the place where Benjamin is now. He is standing before that sea of glass. He is in the presence of the One whose appearance sparkles like jasper and carnelian. He is at home.

But for you, here on earth, the water is not always still. Sometimes it is turbulent. Sometimes the waves of grief make it impossible to see the reflection of God’s face. I know that for Alan and Thao, and for you, Ryan, the last five months have felt like a long, restless journey. You are carrying a weight that the world cannot see. You are living with an absence that feels like a physical presence in the room. I want to tell you the truth: it is okay that the water is not still right now. It is okay that you are tired. God does not demand that you have a perfect, calm surface. He knows the depths of your sorrow. He knows the ache of the heart that misses a son, a brother, a best friend.

There is a profound, quiet beauty in the way Benjamin lived his life. He was a boy who understood that the 'gold coin' he was given—his brilliant mind, his curiosity, his love for aviation, his gentle spirit—was meant to be used, not hidden away in a handkerchief. He was always reaching out. He was always dreaming of 'Con Chim Airlines,' always looking toward the horizon, always ready to share his joy with his family. He lived with his hands open. And that is why he is at peace. He did not hoard his life; he gave it. He gave his smiles, he gave his laughter, he gave his empathy. He was a boy who, in his own way, was always trading in the currency of love.

I want to speak directly to the parents, to Alan and Thao. I know the questions that sometimes arise in the quiet of the night. I know the temptation to look back and wonder if there was something more you could have done, some stone left unturned, some moment missed. But listen to me: the Lord does not come to you to conduct an audit of your failures. He comes to you as the King who says, 'Well done, good and faithful servant.' You were faithful. You were the ones who sat with him, who traveled the world with him, who built a home filled with love and laughter. You did not miss anything. You were the hands and the heart of God for Benjamin, and he knew it. He knew he was loved. That is the only thing that matters. You are not to blame for the sorrow that has come. You are the ones who have been chosen to carry the memory of a beautiful life, and that is a holy, sacred task.

There is a moment in the life of a family that defines them. For you, it is the memory of the way Ben looked at his younger brother, Ryan. It is the way he was always there, shoulder-to-shoulder, sharing the journey. Ryan, you are the keeper of that legacy now. You are the one who knows the inside jokes, the one who remembers the way he giggled, the one who knows the depth of his brotherly love. When you move forward, when you work hard, when you are kind to others, you are not doing it alone. You are doing it with the strength that Ben left behind. He is part of you. He is the wind in your sails. He is the light that helps you see the path ahead.

We must talk about the 'wicked servant' in the parable. He is the one who hid his coin because he was afraid. He was afraid of the master, afraid of the risk, afraid of the loss. Sometimes, when we are grieving, we are tempted to hide our own hearts. We are tempted to bury our love, to keep it 'stored away in a handkerchief' so that it cannot be hurt again. We think that if we stop feeling the pain, we will be safe. But the Gospel tells us that this is not the way of the Kingdom. The way of the Kingdom is to take the love we have and to keep using it, even when it hurts, even when it is risky. We must keep loving, even in our sorrow. We must keep speaking his name. We must keep telling his stories. We must keep the 'Well of Love' flowing, not because it is easy, but because it is the only way to stay connected to the One who gave us the coin in the first place.

Benjamin is now part of that great chorus in the Book of Revelation. He is one of those who stands before the throne, day and night, exclaiming, 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God almighty.' He is not suffering. He is not confused. He is in the light. He is at the banquet. And he is waiting for you. He is watching over you with that same, gentle, knowing smirk he had in the classroom, that same bright smile he had at the restaurant. He is cheering for you. He is the one who knows that the journey is hard, but he also knows that the destination is worth it.

I want to reach out to anyone today who feels like they are in a distant country, far from the joy they once knew. Maybe you are a student struggling to find your way, or a parent holding a child who is suffering, or someone who has lost a loved one and feels like the world has stopped turning. You feel like the servant who has nothing left to trade. But God says to you: 'To everyone who has, more will be given.' Even if all you have is a single, small prayer, give it. Even if all you have is a tear, offer it. God will take that small, broken thing and multiply it. He will turn your mourning into joy. He will turn your emptiness into a vessel for His grace.

Think of the image of the twenty-four elders throwing down their crowns. They recognize that everything they have—their authority, their status, their very lives—comes from the One on the throne. We are called to do the same. We are called to let go of our need to control the outcome, our need to understand the 'why' of our suffering, and simply throw our hearts down before God. We say, 'Lord, it is Yours. All of it. The joy, the sorrow, the memories, the future. It is all Yours.' This is the act of surrender that brings peace. It is the act that allows the 'sea of glass' to become clear again.

Benjamin’s life was a short, brilliant, and beautiful trade. He took the gift of his life and he spent it on love. He spent it on his family. He spent it on his curiosity. He spent it on his kindness. And now, he has received the reward of the faithful. He has been given charge of the cities of light. He is free. And he wants you to be free, too. He wants you to live, to laugh, and to love, even in the midst of your grief. He wants you to know that he is safe, and that you will see him again.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Carry the peace of the Lord. Carry the knowledge that your love for Benjamin is not a dead thing; it is a living, breathing, divine reality. When you wake up tomorrow, and the weight feels heavy, remember that you are carrying the treasure of his memory. Use it. Share it. Let it make you kinder, let it make you more patient, let it make you more aware of the needs of others. Do not hide your heart. Keep it out in the open, where the light of God can touch it, heal it, and transform it.

You are not alone. You are surrounded by the prayers of the Church, by the love of the saints, and by the presence of the One who was, and who is, and who is to come. Benjamin is home. And you are being led there, step by step, one day at a time, held in the arms of the Father who loves you more than you can ever imagine. Rest in that love. Trust in that promise. And know that the story does not end in the grave; it ends in the glory of the throne. Amen.
petitions: For Benjamin Vo and all who have gone before us, that they may rest in the eternal light of Christ’s presence, we pray to the Lord.
For all who grieve, especially Alan, Thao, and Ryan, that God may console them with His peace and grant them the hope of the resurrection, we pray to the Lord.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of His face shine upon you forever. Go in peace.

readings.label: Tusaajaujuq 1
readings.text: Uvanga, John, takujalaurpunga angmaumajumik matu qilangmut, tusaalaurlungalu niqituinnaqtuq nipaa uqautijaujuq uvamnut siuliani, uqaqtuq: 'Aitaugiit, takujunnarniarapkit qanuq pivalliajut.' Unuinnak anirniup iluani katuttaugama. Iniqtivik qilangmi, iniqtivikmi iksivajuq kikkutuinnait takujaujuq jasper-tut carnelian-tut. Iniqtivik qitiani emerald-tut takujaujuq. Iniqtivikmi qulirijavut 24-nik iniqtiviknik, 24-nik angajukqaanik iksivajunik, qirniqtuqannitut qaqurtunik annuraanik, uviuvillu qukiqtuqanik. Iniqtivikmit, qaujimajavut qaujimajavut qaujimajavut. 7 ikumajut qaujimajavut iniqtivikmi, 7-ngujut anirniit Ataniup. Iniqtivikmi takujaujuq crystal-tut takujaujuq. Qitiani, iniqtivikmi, 4-ngujut inuujut takujaujut, takujaujut takujaujut. Sivulliq inuujut lion-tut, aippaa calf-tut, pingajuat inuup takujaujuq, tisamangat eagle-tut. 4-ngujut inuujut, 6-nik suluujut, takujaujut. Ulluq unnulu, uqaqtuq: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God almighty, who was, and who is, and who is to come.' Kikkut inuujut quviasuktut, 24-ngujut angajukqaat nunaqtuq, iksivajunut, quviasuktut, uqaqtuq: 'Worthy are you, Lord our God, to receive glory and honor and power, for you created all things; because of your will they came to be and were created.'

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: Kikkut Jesus-mik tusaajut, uqaqtuq, Jesus Jerusalem-mi, Kingdom of God-mik uqallaktuq. Uqaqtuq: 'Nobleman-ngujut aullalaurtuq, angajukqaangunirmut. 10-ngujut kikkut ikajurtaujut, 10-ngujut gold-mik tunijaujut, uqaqtuq: 'Atuqlugit utiqpata.' Kikkut uqallaktut, 'Pijumangittavut.' Utiqpat, kikkut ikajurtaujut, uqaqtuq: 'Qanuq pivalliajut?' Sivulliq uqaqtuq: '10-ngujut pivalliajut.' Uqaqtuq: 'Well done, good servant! 10 cities-nik ataniujut.' Aippaa uqaqtuq: '5-ngujut pivalliajut.' Uqaqtuq: '5 cities-nik ataniujut.' Pingajuat uqaqtuq: 'Gold-mik atuniarpunga, kinguani, kappiagivagit.' Uqaqtuq: 'Wicked servant! Bank-mi ikinngittut? Interest-ngujut utiqpata.' Kikkut uqallaktut, 'Take from him, give to 10-ngujut.' Uqaqtuq: 'Everyone who has, more will be given, but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away.' Kikkut enemies-ngujut, slay them.' Taimanna, Jerusalem-mut aullalaurtuq.

standing_petitions: Benjamin Vo-mut, kikkullu tuqusimajunut, Kristusiup qaujimajaujuani inuujut.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.
Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
